ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a schematic mountain profile. A is near the lower mountain area on the left, B is at the valley position to its right, and C is near a higher ridge farther to the right; the slope area between B and C is marked with shading and labeled "shaded area," indicating that noon sunlight cannot reach it. Then reason: The question stem states that place A is located due south of place B, and A is on the left of B in the figure, so from left to right in the figure can be understood as from south to north. In this way, the shaded slope between B and C is a south-facing slope that inclines southward. On December 22, the Sun is directly overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn; if this place is located south of the Tropic of Capricorn, then the noon Sun is located to the north, and the south-facing slope is a shaded slope, easily forming a shaded area. From this it is judged that this area should be in the Southern Hemisphere and south of the Tropic of Capricorn, most likely near 30°S.
